subject: Preflight: NebulaAI scaling profile deep-dive
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina@nebula.ai>; product@nebula.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Preflight: NebulaAI scaling profile deep-dive

Hi Lina / Nebula product team,

Thanks for taking the time to do a preflight with us. To make our dedicated sizing and GPU footprint recommendation accurate, we need a concise traffic profile and a few workload details from your side. I attached a small CSV template for sample telemetry (sizing_intake_template.csv) — if you can populate the sample rows from a typical weekday and a recent spike day that would be ideal.

Main asks:
- Typical QPS range and P95/P99 latencies for your user-facing endpoints (last 30 days).
- Prompt / response length distributions (tokens) per endpoint or feature (e.g., chat: prompt 50-200 tokens, response 150-800 tokens).
- Session behavior: are requests mostly independent or do you maintain long-lived sessions with KV cache reuse / streaming? If session affinity exists, roughly how many requests per session and average session duration.
- Peak burst profile: expected concurrent sessions/requests during your largest 5-minute window (and whether you can tolerate ~200–300ms additional latency for batching).
- Model variants used in production and whether lower-quantized variants acceptable for fallback.

Initial constraints we should be aware of: latency SLO target 100–150ms p50 for interactive features, and a cost cap per 1k responses that Procurement will want to hold us to.

If you prefer, we can run a quick 60-minute workshop to walk through the telemetry together — I recommend including an engineer who can pull token-length histograms. Proposed times: Wed 29 Jun 09:00–11:00 PT or Thu 30 Jun 14:00–16:00 PT.

Next steps from our side once we have the data: we’ll run a micro-sizer, propose a Dedicated fleet mix (GPU SKUs and oversubscription targets), and surface fallback routing policies and estimated monthly cost ranges.

Thanks —
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

Attachment: sizing_intake_template.csv (CSV template with timestamped QPS, avg_tokens_prompt, avg_tokens_response, session_id_sample column)
From: Lina Gomez <lina@nebula.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@nebula.ai, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:34:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Preflight: NebulaAI scaling profile deep-dive

Avery —

Thanks for the clear checklist. I filled out the attached sample telemetry (nebula_traffic_snapshot.csv) with two representative days: one normal and one spike (launch day). Quick answers inline:
- Typical QPS: 8–22 overall, with p95 latency ~180ms (API edge + our app code). Spike day peaked at 320 QPS sustained for ~7 minutes.
- Token distributions (approx): chat_prompt median 60 tokens, chat_response median 420 tokens; summarization prompt median 120 tokens, response median 60 tokens.
- Sessions: we keep session affinity for chat (KV reuse) — avg 6 requests per session, mean session duration ~4.5 minutes. We do use streaming for responses in the web client.
- Peak burst tolerance: we can tolerate extra latency up to ~300ms for brief spikes but Procurement wants a backup plan if falling back to a smaller model increases error rates.
- Models: primary is an open LlamaX-70B (quantized to q4f16 in prod), fallback to 13B variants for extreme burst.

Open questions for you: 1) How would Redwood handle KV cache when routing between dedicated and fallback model variants? 2) Any recommendations on session pool sizes to preserve KV reuse while keeping cost predictable?

Attaching: nebula_traffic_snapshot.csv

Best,
Lina Gomez
Head of Product Operations | NebulaAI
lina@nebula.ai | +1 628-555-0199
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina@nebula.ai>, product@nebula.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preflight: NebulaAI scaling profile deep-dive

Lina — thanks for the snapshot and the details, this is exactly the data we need. Quick responses to your questions and proposed next steps below.

1) KV cache + routing: our smart routing preserves session affinity by hashing on your session_id and preferring pinned dedicated machines that already hold the KV state. If we need to route to a fallback 13B model, we can warm the KV by streaming the last N tokens (configurable); there is a brief cold-warm penalty but we have a warming policy that keeps tail latency bounded for short bursts. We’ll include an occupancy plan that quantifies warm-up token costs.

2) Session pool sizing: initial recommendation based on your averages — reserve pool slots to support ~30% of concurrent sessions (so KV reuse stays high) while using elastic burst capacity for the remainder. For your peak of 320 QPS and avg 6 requests/session, that suggests a pool sized for ~35–45 dedicated session slots per GPU for the 70B footprint; Karthik will run a micro-simulation and return concrete GPU/slot numbers and cost bands.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Karthik: run micro-sizer simulations against nebula_traffic_snapshot.csv and produce 3 fleet mixes (conservative, balanced, cost-optimized) with estimated monthly spend — target by Thu 25 Jun EOD.
- Schedule a 60-minute workshop to review the sizing results and walk through fallback/kv warm strategies. Lina, would Wed 29 Jun 09:00 PT work for you?
- I’ll upload a working doc with the simulation notes and baseline assumptions here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-nebula-scaling-doc (placeholder link).

If that plan looks good I’ll convert this thread into a short mutual action plan in HubSpot.

Thanks —
Avery
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---
Marissa & Karthik: I’m marking this as high-priority for pre-sales sizing. Karthik, please include quantization trade-offs and an appendix that lists the assumptions for latency vs. cost under each fleet mix.

Attachment: redwood_sizer_notes.pdf (outline of simulation assumptions and initial sizing knobs)
